title: Critical CSS
definition: A technique that extracts the CSS for above-the-fold content and inlines it directly into the HTML document, while deferring the rest of the CSS.
simpleExplanation: When a user visits your site, they only see the top 20% of the page (the hero banner and navigation). They don't see the footer until they scroll down. Critical CSS grabs ONLY the CSS needed to paint that top 20%, shoves it directly into the HTML `<head>`, and loads the footer CSS later. This makes the website appear instantly on the screen.
realWorldExample: Getting a perfect 100/100 score on Google PageSpeed Insights. Without Critical CSS, the browser stares at a blank white screen for 2 seconds while it downloads the massive `styles.css` file.

basic: Where does Critical CSS go in the HTML document?
intermediate: If Critical CSS is so good, why not inline the entire `styles.css` file?

answers.question: Where does it go?
answers.answer: It is written inside a `<style>` tag directly in the `<head>` of the HTML.

answers.question: Why not inline everything?
answers.answer: Because external CSS files can be cached by the browser. If the user visits a second page on your site, the browser instantly loads the cached `.css` file from their hard drive. If you inline EVERYTHING into the HTML, the user has to re-download the massive CSS chunk on every single page they visit.
